RagShortTexts: Joachim of Fiore's prophecy that the Age of the Spirit would commence in 1260 ignited.

Variants.Content: Abbot Joachim of Fiore, who died in 1202, divided world history into three ages: the Age of the Father under Law, the Age of the Son under Grace, and a final Age of the Holy Spirit that his followers expected around 1260. His writings were copied widely, and their numerological schemes gave believers a calendar of the end. In late 1259, news of Mongol devastation in the east and strange portents at home stirred apocalyptic fear across Christendom. The coming age promised a church without the old sacramental hierarchy, and that promise was sharpened by the corruption of many clergy. The papal curia watched the prophecy closely, since its supporters challenged the order of bishops and monasteries, and extreme preachers were silenced when they predicted the end of the sacraments.

Radical Spiritual Franciscans embraced Joachimite prophecies, preaching that corrupt clerical hierarchies would wither before voluntary apostolic poverty in 1260. The Curia watches warily, censuring extremists who predict the obsolescence of church sacraments.

Barefoot flagellants march through marketplace mud whipping their shoulders bloody, crying that judgment comes in 1260. Common folk crowd into parish chapels, weeping for mercy before the sky turns red.
